memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: So Abram went up from Egypt to the Negev, with his wife and everything he had, and Lot went with him. Abram had become very wealthy in livestock and in silver and gold. - Gen 13:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Abram leaves Egypt - the place of his failure - and heads back toward the land God had given him. Notice the direction: he "went up from Egypt." In Scripture, going down to Egypt is nearly always a step away from God's provision; coming up out of Egypt is a return. Abram is retracing his steps back to where he should have stayed.

And Scripture notes, almost pointedly, that he had become "very wealthy." He left Egypt richer than he entered. But wealth gained in a season of compromise is not the same as blessing. As we'll see in this very chapter, that wealth would soon cause trouble in his own household. What we gain outside God's will often costs us later.

There is grace here, though. Abram is going back. He does not stay in Egypt licking his wounds or hiding in shame. He turns around. That is what repentance looks like - not merely feeling sorry, but walking back to where you left God.

If you have wandered into your own Egypt, the road back is open. God does not require you to fix everything first; He simply calls you to turn around and come. "Return to me, and I will return to you," says the Lord (Zech 1:3). The journey back may be long, but it always leads home.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Is there an "Egypt" you need to leave and journey back from?
- Have you mistaken gain for God's blessing?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, thank You that the road back to You is always open. Where I have wandered, turn me around. Help me leave my Egypt behind and journey home to You.
Amen.
